Subject: Sharp latency + 5xx spike in AZ3 — urgent

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden jump in user-facing latency and an increase in 5xx rates from our AZ3 (east-us-3) footprint starting ~07:45 PT. P95 latency is up ~4x, error rate at ~6% sustained for the last 15m, and throughput is saturating. We've attached a short error sample and the raw metrics export. This is impacting our checkout flows (high-value traffic).

Can you confirm whether you can fail traffic to us-west-4 and whether there are any model/variant compatibility issues we should expect? Immediate remediation is required — please advise on ETA.

Regards,
Jane Doe

Jane — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're on it. Immediate plan (next steps):

1) SRE (Hannah) will triage and surface root-cause within 20m.
2) If saturation/infra limits are confirmed, we'll execute a geo-evacuation from AZ3 -> us-west-4 and enable the degraded-mode routing policy to keep latencies stable.
3) We'll also spin a temporary lower-memory model variant (quantized) for Copperbridge traffic as a fallback to reduce KVCACHE pressure.

Rishi / Execs: we will need a priority routing pin and temporary capacity bump for one maintenance window (~30–45m) and discretionary credit approval for the impacted window if failover impacts quality. I need confirmation to proceed with the evac (manual approval requested).

Jane — we will keep you updated every 10 minutes. ETA for initial mitigation attempt: ~25m.

- Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Sharp latency + 5xx spike in AZ3 — urgent

Quick tech update (initial triage):

- Symptoms: sustained queue length growth on AZ3 inference pools serving Copperbridge (q-depth > 2500), KV-cache eviction churn increased sharply, OOM throttles observed on several nodes. Autoscaling did not react quickly due to burst profile and a bug in the scale-up cooldown logic (tracked).
- Impact surface: highest on routes using long-context sessions; throughput-critical checkout endpoints hit >5% 5xx.
- Short-term mitigation (recommended):
  * Activate geo-evacuation rule to steer 60% of traffic to us-west-4 in controlled batches (start with 30% -> 60% over 10 minutes).
  * Enable degraded execution variant (redwood-small-quant) for Copperbridge pin to lower memory per-infer and reduce KV churn.
  * Start graceful drain on AZ3 pods for non-priority classes.
  * If allowed, request manual override on our routing controller to prioritize Copperbridge for a 45m window.

If we proceed now we expect P95 to drop toward baseline within 12–18 minutes after the initial 30% shift and <1% 5xx within 30–45 minutes. Risks: small quality regressions with quantized variant; we'll monitor inference divergence on a control sample.

- Hannah Schmitt
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

2) Legal/Procurement: Marissa, can you confirm whether a manual priority override (routing pin) requires a contractual exception for Copperbridge? If yes, we'll need Procurement looped.

I approve the technical plan pending 1 & 2 above. If we get the green light, Hannah proceed with staged evac. I'll notify CRO and CEO after we start the shift.

- Rishi Malhotra
